verdict.rationale: Sentry's platform docs say users with uncovered use cases can find documentation on reporting events themselves, and they describe a large community-supported SDK ecosystem. Both point to an ingestion path that non-official clients can use. However, the evidence never shows the protocol specification itself (event or envelope payload schema, DSN and auth header format, ingestion endpoints), so how documented and open it is remains unproven. missing for 10: an explicit published ingestion/envelope protocol spec, documented auth and endpoint details for custom clients, and hands-on confirmation of a custom client sending events.

support.subject: As a developer, the event-ingestion protocol is documented and open enough that custom clients and compatible SDKs can send events without an official SDK

citations.quote: If your use case is very specific, or not covered by Sentry, you'll find documentation on how to report events on your own using our SDK API.
there’s also a large ecosystem supported by the community
